grader.scene_detector: ffmpeg scdet, threshold 10.0 (the filter's own default)

categories.name: hook_window
categories.why: Short-form viewers commit or leave in the opening moments, so a hook that starts later than about two seconds, or runs long without resolving, has already spent the attention it was meant to buy.

categories.name: cut_cadence
categories.why: A short holds attention by changing what is on screen, but a longer clip needs a calmer rhythm than a very short one, so the workable range of cuts per ten seconds narrows as the clip gets longer.

categories.name: duration_fit
categories.why: Below roughly seven seconds there is no room to pay a hook off, and past about a minute a short-form clip stops being one thing a viewer watches whole.

categories.name: structure_completeness
categories.why: Beat roles are an authoring fact, not a pixel fact: nothing in an encoded video says which shot was meant as hook, development, or payoff. Grade the timeline to measure this.

categories.name: text_density
categories.why: Reading on-screen text out of pixels needs OCR, which v0 does not ship. Grade the timeline instead, where the text is declared rather than inferred.
